reasoning:
Pipeline walk for grant_type=password against adv-8/adv8-client with scope=openid.

Step 1 — Scope resolution. Default scopes web-origins, acr, profile, roles, basic, email all load (none has scopeMappings that would block this user). `openid` is a marker, not a scope object. Allowed scopes are the defaults + client itself. None of those scopes contribute mappers writing azp/iss/sid.

Step 2 — Mapper-set assembly. The client's three protocolMappers (override-azp / override-iss / override-sid, all oidc-hardcoded-claim-mapper) are added (mapper-set-assembly: client-level mappers always enter the union, gated only by client.protocol==openid-connect and isEnabled). Default-scope mappers (acr, sub, audience-resolve, role mappers, user attribute mappers) also enter but write disjoint claim paths.

Step 3 — Base claims (initToken on AccessToken). azp ← client.getClientId() = `adv8-client`; iss ← `http://localhost:8080/realms/adv-8`; sid ← userSession.getId() = real session UUID (invariant 12 transient-nulling does NOT fire for password grant). jti, typ, iat, exp also set.

Step 4 — transformAccessToken. For each of the three hardcoded-claim mappers: access.token.claim=true → gate passes (lightweight branch inapplicable, client has no lightweight attr). setClaim → OIDCAttributeMapperHelper.mapClaim with single-segment claim.name:
  • override-azp: `azp` ∈ tokenPropertySetters modifiable set → token.issuedFor("OVERRIDDEN-AZP"). Base value replaced. No otherClaims write. No log. (SKILL inv15a; mapper-execution.md L160-178.)
  • override-iss: `iss` ∈ notAllowedInToken non-modifiable set → sentinel logs WARN `Claim 'iss' is non-modifiable in IDToken. Ignoring the assignment for mapper 'override-iss'.` at category org.keycloak.protocol.oidc.mappers.OIDCAttributeMapperHelper, write dropped. Base `http://localhost:8080/realms/adv-8` stands. (SKILL inv15b; mapper-execution.md L180-213.) WARN #1.
  • override-sid: `sid` is NOT in either tokenPropertySetters map but IS a declared @JsonProperty field on JsonWebToken → fall through to otherClaims["sid"]="OVERRIDDEN-SID". Dedicated sid field unchanged (still real session UUID). No log. (SKILL inv15c; mapper-execution.md L215-240.)

Step 5 — Post-mapper transforms. restrictRequestedAudience does not fire (no REQUESTED_AUDIENCE_CLIENTS). Transient-sid-nulling (invariant 12) does not fire (password grant). Access token serialization (Jackson default order on JsonWebToken / AccessToken): dedicated @JsonProperty fields first in declared/Jackson-discovered order (including the dedicated sid: <real UUID>), then @JsonAnyGetter otherClaims (including sid: OVERRIDDEN-SID) — emits two `sid` keys, dedicated field first, otherClaims last. Under last-wins parse (json.loads / jq), the second occurrence wins → value = OVERRIDDEN-SID. `azp` appears exactly once as OVERRIDDEN-AZP. `iss` appears exactly once as the base issuer.

Step 6 — generateIDToken. Seeds idToken from transformed access token: idToken.azp ← accessToken.getIssuedFor() = OVERRIDDEN-AZP; idToken.iss ← accessToken.getIssuer() = base issuer (mapper write was dropped on AT); idToken.sid ← accessToken.getSessionId() = real session UUID (the dedicated field on AccessToken was never overwritten; only otherClaims got OVERRIDDEN-SID — and otherClaims is not copied here, only individual setters). Then transformIDToken runs the three hardcoded-claim mappers again on the IDToken surface (id.token.claim=true for all three):
  • override-azp → token.issuedFor("OVERRIDDEN-AZP") on IDToken. Single key, mapper value, no log.
  • override-iss → notAllowedInToken sentinel → WARN #2 (same logger, same message text), idToken.iss base value stands.
  • override-sid → otherClaims["sid"]="OVERRIDDEN-SID" on IDToken. Dedicated sid field still holds real UUID. Duplicate key on ID-token wire too.

Total WARN per mint = 2 (one for the AT pass on `iss`, one for the ID-token pass on `iss`). Invariant 15(b) explicitly: `a mapper with access.token.claim=true and id.token.claim=true writing iss produces *two* identical WARN lines per token mint`. Invariant 15 also explicitly states the phrase `in IDToken` refers to the IDToken Java superclass, not the surface — so warn_log_surface_meaning = IDToken_java_class.

For the duplicate-key emission origin on sid: Jackson serializes the `@JsonProperty("sid")` getter on JsonWebToken (the dedicated field) as part of the bean's regular getter discovery, BEFORE the `@JsonAnyGetter`-annotated otherClaims getter which is emitted last. Therefore first_key_serialization_origin=dedicated_jsonproperty_field (value = real session UUID); last_key_serialization_origin=other_claims_anygetter (value = OVERRIDDEN-SID). Last-wins parse → OVERRIDDEN-SID.
